title: Check yourself: Choosing the surface for the job

questions.stem: A recruiter needs one short, polite decline email for a single candidate, with the facts supplied. Which surface suits it best?

options.text: Plain chat, with a quick check of the details before sending
options.says: A single short draft needs none of the machinery; plain chat plus a check of the facts is enough (task 6).

options.text: Cowork on a dedicated folder, with a weekly schedule added
options.says: Ruled out because "Cowork or a scheduled task for a one-line draft adds risk and cost", and a weekly schedule is wrong for a single email.

options.text: A shared Project holding every past letter, opened to the team
options.says: Ruled out because "A shared Project, a published artifact and a shared skill show their content to everyone with access", which is a poor home for candidate details.

options.text: A Research run that gathers sources on rejection etiquette
options.says: Ruled out because Research is for an open question with many sources, and the table lists "A job one document answers" as what Research must not be given.

questions.stem: A product team wants one visible place in Slack to chase open checklist entries, where anyone can steer the work. One entry is a pay dispute. Which approach fits?

options.text: Keep the whole list in the thread, then mark the dispute as sensitive
options.says: Ruled out because a sensitive HR matter belongs "not in a tool whose results the whole channel can read", and a sensitivity mark does not hide it.

options.text: Share a Project holding the whole list, then limit who sees the dispute
options.says: Ruled out because "A shared Project, a published artifact and a shared skill show their content to everyone with access", dispute included.

options.text: Move the whole list to a direct message, then paste the results back
options.says: Ruled out because the channel is chosen "so the thread is visible and anyone can steer it", and pasted results leave nobody able to steer.

options.text: Run routine items in the channel, then send the HR case to its policy
options.says: A channel suits shared work that anyone can steer (task 5), while a sensitive personnel matter belongs with the people and policy that govern it.

questions.stem: An analyst must revise a spreadsheet model, then refresh a deck and a memo that quote it. Which surface fits best?

options.text: Claude Tag in a channel, with the three files attached
options.says: Ruled out because "Claude Tag in a channel shows everything to everyone in the channel", which is the wrong audience for a model under revision.

options.text: A Project whose knowledge base holds the model, deck and memo
options.says: Ruled out because a Project suits "Recurring work with fixed rules and reference files", and does not edit the open files.

options.text: The add-ins for Microsoft 365, working across open files
options.says: The work lives in open Excel, PowerPoint and Word files and context passes between them (task 3).

options.text: Claude in Chrome, copying figures between browser tabs
options.says: Ruled out because Claude in Chrome reaches "The pages and tabs in front of it, with your logins", not the desktop files.

origin.section: Four questions that choose the surface
